takes.p: Collectors read the copyright page first, for the printing line and the date. Try it the other way round once. Read the book, decide whether it was any good, and only then find out what it is worth. The order changes what you remember about it.

Paperback horror was marketed on its art, and a great many of the books never lived up to their covers. That is not a scandal; it is the business. But it does mean the art deserves its own credit, and its own scholarship, separate from whatever the prose inside managed.

There is no such thing as a guilty pleasure on this shelf. There are books that are good, books that are fun, and books that are both. Plenty of the paperbacks we collect were written fast, for rent money, by professionals. Treat them as professional work and they read better.
